lesson.title: Calling the Class: How Instantiation Builds an Object
lesson.summary: Instantiation is the process that runs when you call a class like a function: Python creates a new, empty object, runs __init__ on it to set it up, and hands you back the finished object, all from that one line of code.
lesson.body:
Writing Dog("Rex", "Labrador") looks like an ordinary function call, but three distinct things happen behind that single line. First, Python creates a brand new, empty object of type Dog. Second, Python calls the class's __init__ method, automatically passing that new object in as self, along with whatever arguments you supplied, so the object's attributes get set up. Third, Python hands the fully initialized object back to you, which is what actually ends up stored in the variable on the left of the equals sign. This whole process, from calling the class to receiving a ready-to-use object, is called instantiation, and each time you do it, you get a completely separate object, even if you pass in the exact same arguments twice.

```python
class Dog:
    def __init__(self, name, breed):
        self.name = name
        self.breed = breed
        print(f"Creating a Dog object for {name}")

rex = Dog("Rex", "Labrador")
fido = Dog("Fido", "Poodle")

print(type(rex) is Dog)
print(isinstance(fido, Dog))
print(rex.name, fido.name)
```

```
Creating a Dog object for Rex
Creating a Dog object for Fido
True
True
Rex Fido
```

Each call to Dog(...) triggers its own run of __init__, which is why "Creating a Dog object for Rex" prints during the first call and "Creating a Dog object for Fido" prints during the second, in that order, right when each instantiation happens. Afterward, both type(rex) is Dog and isinstance(fido, Dog) confirm that each result really is a Dog object, and rex.name and fido.name confirm they kept their own separate data, exactly as the previous concept on objects described.

It is worth being precise about the vocabulary at this point: Dog is the class, the blueprint; rex and fido are objects, or instances, of that class; and instantiation is the act of calling Dog(...) that produced each one. Everything an object knows about itself immediately after instantiation comes from what __init__ assigned to it, which brings us to a close look at exactly what those assigned values are.
